continuous_text.title: The Classroom Song
continuous_text.content:
Good morning, class.
Good morning to you!
How are you?
I'm fine, thank you.
What is it? It's an eraser.
What is it? It's a ruler.
What is it? It's a pencil.
What is it? It's a crayon.
Now pick up your pen
And open your book.
Say the words
And write with me.
Let's start now. 1, 2, 3!
Chorus

continuous_text.title: Classroom Colors
continuous_text.content:
Frame 1:
Teacher: Look, Tim. What is it?
Tim: It's a pen.
Frame 2:
Tim: Look! What are they?
Teacher: They're pencils.
Tim: Yes, they're yellow pencils.
Frame 3:
Teacher: And what is it?
Tim: It's a marker. A red marker.
Teacher: Yes! Good, Tim.
Frame 4:
Teacher: And what are they?
Tim: They're erasers.
Teacher: And what color are they?
Frame 5:
Tim: They're red.
Teacher: Red? No, Tim. They're green erasers.
Frame 6:
Teacher: Tim!
Tim: No, look! They're red erasers.
continuous_text.notes: Frames 1-4 on page 12; frames 5-6 on page 13; track 24

continuous_text.title: Culture Connection: Classrooms Around the World
continuous_text.content:
1 In the United States of America, I have a big classroom. My desk is small, and my chair is small, too. I have a pencil case, and I have markers, pencils, and crayons. I have an eraser and a ruler, too.
2 My classroom in China is big. My desk is big, too. I have a pen and a notebook. I have a tablet and a green pencil sharpener.
3 This is my classroom in Africa. It's small. I have a small desk. I have a black backpack and a yellow pencil. I have notebooks, too.

curriculum_components.title: Good Morning, Class!
curriculum_components.description: Presentation and recognition of 10 classroom objects.

curriculum_components.title: The Classroom Song
curriculum_components.description: Song contextualizing classroom objects and greeting routines.

curriculum_components.title: Classroom Colors
curriculum_components.description: Six-frame comic story practicing singular/plural object identification and colors.

curriculum_components.title: Language in Action
curriculum_components.description: Practice with 'What is it? It's a...' and 'What are they? They're...'.

curriculum_components.title: School possessions
curriculum_components.description: Counting possessions and reading inventory descriptions.

curriculum_components.title: My Pencil Case poster
curriculum_components.description: Creating and presenting a poster about student's pencil case possessions.

curriculum_components.title: Grammar (Sit down! Don't run!)
curriculum_components.description: Affirmative and negative imperatives for classroom rules.

curriculum_components.title: Classrooms
curriculum_components.description: Classroom environments in Africa, the USA, and China.

curriculum_components.title: Be polite.
curriculum_components.description: Practicing polite classroom interactions using 'Thank you', 'You're welcome', and 'Please sit down'.

curriculum_components.title: a, t, p, n
curriculum_components.description: Letter-sound correspondence and sound blending for a, t, p, n.

curriculum_components.title: Review
curriculum_components.description: Consolidation of Unit 1 vocabulary, grammar, and structures.

curriculum_components.title: Self-assessment
curriculum_components.description: Student self-assessment checklist of unit goals.

schema_gaps.observed_content: Think Big breakout prompt feature appearing across multiple lesson pages (e.g., pp. 11, 13, 16, 21, 22).
schema_gaps.problem: Think Big is a distinct higher-order thinking / critical thinking sub-feature often attached to standard activities, but currently must be modeled as a standard activity or notes field.
schema_gaps.proposed_change: Add an optional 'sub_feature_type' field to activity records (e.g. 'think_big', 'project', 'i_can').
schema_gaps.reason: Allows analytical grouping and filtering of critical thinking prompts across units.
